newsitem.title: JAPAN: Disclosure rules urged for foreign remittances - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Disclosure rules urged for foreign remittances - MOF.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) on Wednesday submitted a proposal recommending that disclosure rules be imposed on cross-border transactions after reform of Japan's foreign exchange law, a MOF tax official said.
But he added that further details remain undecided.

When asked about a Yomiuri Shimbun article that said the proposal would recommend imposing rules requiring that any cross-border foreign exchange transaction of one million yen or above be reported to tax authorities, the official said he could not give a specific amount.

"For example, the United States only requires disclosures of foreign remittances once they reach a certain amount. We would bring our disclosure rules into line with those in foreign countries," he added.
These new regulations would be in conjunction with a general overhaul of Japan's foreign exchange law which, if passed by parliament, would come into effect in 1998, the official said.
The disclosure rule would be an attempt to prevent tax evasion and money laundering, the official said.
"It seems possible that these actions may increase once foreign exchange laws become more liberal, so some sort of disclosure rule appears to be a necessary thing," he added.
Many industrialised nations, such as the United States, have no comprehensive foreign exchange laws controlling currency or capital transactions.
